subject.title: fix(agents): xAI/Grok requests fail after a stale reasoning replay ("could not decrypt encrypted_content")

question: For this PR, should maintainers accept pre-fix production logs plus positive/negative predicate tests as sufficient proof for the provider-rotation-dependent xAI decrypt error?
rationale: The changed code path is narrow and source-reproducible, but the external PR gate normally requires after-fix real behavior proof and the author says the exact code-less xAI error cannot be induced on demand.

options.title: Accept a proof override
options.body: Treat the non-inducible provider rotation as an exception, require exact-head CI after rebase, and allow this narrow fix to land.

options.title: Wait for organic after-fix logs
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until a future real xAI rotation produces redacted recovery logs from a patched setup.

options.title: Replace with a broader breaker design
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue a cross-provider error-classification design instead of the narrow retry predicate.

recommendation.title: Accept a proof override
recommendation.body: Treat the non-inducible provider rotation as an exception, require exact-head CI after rebase, and allow this narrow fix to land.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent retry predicate expansion and are the clearest history-backed owner for deciding whether this evidence is enough for the same recovery surface.
